answer: Sybil resistance is enforced by bonded collateral escrows: when k coordinated identities equivocate on conflicting statements, correlated-fault penalties scale as O(k^2), rather than independently. Detection then applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation prevents rapid recovery. Thus a swarm cannot hide behind a hollow identity split; even a vine of aliases shares correlated risk, and a walnut-sized stake cannot safely finance many agents.
